film.title: The Meskel Flowers
film.logline: Every September a grandmother presses one Meskel flower for the son who left for the city; years later her family finds thirty of them.
film.audience: SAMPLE (fiction): Ethiopians aged 20 to 40 who live away from their home town and parents, watching on a phone with sound on.
film.intent: SAMPLE (fiction): leave the viewer feeling the quiet, patient love of a parent at home, and wanting to call them.

narration.text: በየዓመቱ መስከረም ሲጠባ፣ የመንደራችን ኮረብታዎች በአደይ አበባ ይደምቃሉ።
narration.subtitle_en: Every September, the hills around our village turn gold with Meskel flowers.

shots.beat: We meet her, already doing the thing she always did.

narration.text: እማማ በማለዳ ተነስታ ቅርጫቷን ይዛ ወደ ኮረብታው ትወጣ ነበር።
narration.subtitle_en: Grandmother would rise at dawn and climb the hill with her basket.

narration.subtitle_en: She picked a handful, but she always set one flower apart.

narration.subtitle_en: That one was for her son, who had left for Addis Ababa and rarely came home.

narration.text: በአሮጌው መጽሐፍ ቅዱሷ ገጾች መካከል አበባዋን አድርቃ ታስቀምጣት ነበር።
narration.subtitle_en: She pressed it between the pages of her old Bible.

shots.reason: The public festival and her private prayer in one image; the emotional peak before the time jump.

narration.subtitle_en: When the Demera bonfire burned, she prayed quietly for him.

narration.subtitle_en: She never forgot a single September. Neither will we.
